newsitem.title: JAPAN: Daihatsu sees higher 1997 domestic sales.
newsitem.headline: Daihatsu sees higher 1997 domestic sales.

text.p: Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd said on Thursday it forecast its domestic sales in calendar 1997 at 500,000 vehicles, up 6.6 percent from the previous year.
In 1996, Daihatsu, Japan's second-biggest manufacturer of 660cc minivehicles, recorded a 13.8 percent rise to 469,237.
Domestic sales projections for 1997 included 450,000 660cc mini vehicles, up from 444,432 a year earlier.
Daihatsu forecast its vehicle exports at 105,000 vehicles in 1997, up 66.4 percent from last year, fuelled largely by rising exports to Europe. Exports fell 17.5 percent in 1996.
Daihatsu this month started exporting its 850cc Move and 1500cc Pyzar recreational vehicles at a monthly rate of 1,000 Moves and 800 Pyzars.

Daihatsu's exports of vehicle kits for overseas assembly were projected to fall 12.8 percent in 1997 to 235,000, as local procurement at its Chinese production facility had already reached nearly 100 percent. Export kits last year rose 6.5 percent to 269,460.
